de: Das Modell liest ausgewählte Quellen und Anweisungen, die zum Schreiben und Prüfen des Dokuments nötig sind.

Es kann Ziel, Zielgruppe, Struktur oder Vorlage, ausgewählte Dokumente und Analysen, Tabellen, Bilder, Notizen, Aussagen, Nachweise und Referenzen erhalten. Enthalten die Quellen Namen, Mandanteninformationen oder geschäftliche, rechtliche oder finanzielle Daten, können diese gelesen werden, wenn sie für Text oder Nachweisprüfung nötig sind.

Entwurf, erzeugte Tabellen und gerendertes Dokument können zur Korrektur von Inhalt, Referenzen und Kohärenz erneut vom Modell gelesen werden. Dokumentwerkzeuge erstellen und prüfen DOCX- oder PDF-Ausgaben mechanisch; sie genehmigen keine fachlichen Schlussfolgerungen. Weitergabe, Upload oder Lieferung an den Mandanten erfolgen nicht automatisch.
en: The model reads selected sources and instructions needed to write and review the document.

It may receive the objective, audience, structure or template, selected documents and analyses, tables, images, notes, claims, evidence, and references. If the sources contain names, client information, or commercial, legal, or financial data, those elements may be read when needed for the text or evidence review.

The draft, generated tables, and rendered document may be read again by the model to correct content, references, and coherence. Document tools create and mechanically inspect DOCX or PDF output; they do not approve professional conclusions. Sharing, uploading, or delivering the document to a client is not automatic.
es: El modelo lee las fuentes seleccionadas y las instrucciones necesarias para redactar y revisar el documento.

Puede recibir objetivo, público, estructura o plantilla, documentos y análisis seleccionados, tablas, imágenes, notas, afirmaciones, evidencias y referencias. Si las fuentes contienen nombres, información del cliente o datos comerciales, jurídicos o financieros, esos elementos pueden leerse cuando sean necesarios para el texto o la revisión de evidencias.

El modelo puede volver a leer el borrador, las tablas generadas y el documento renderizado para corregir contenido, referencias y coherencia. Las herramientas documentales crean y comprueban mecánicamente DOCX o PDF; no aprueban conclusiones profesionales. Compartir, cargar o entregar el documento al cliente no es automático.
fr: Le modèle lit les sources sélectionnées et les instructions nécessaires pour rédiger et réviser le document.

Il peut recevoir objectif, public, structure ou modèle, documents et analyses sélectionnés, tableaux, images, notes, affirmations, preuves et références. Si les sources contiennent des noms, informations client ou données commerciales, juridiques ou financières, ces éléments peuvent être lus lorsqu'ils sont nécessaires au texte ou à la vérification des preuves.

Le projet, les tableaux générés et le document rendu peuvent être relus par le modèle afin de corriger contenu, références et cohérence. Les outils documentaires créent et contrôlent mécaniquement les sorties DOCX ou PDF ; ils n'approuvent pas les conclusions professionnelles. Partage, envoi ou remise au client ne sont pas automatiques.
it: Il modello legge le fonti selezionate e le istruzioni necessarie a scrivere e rivedere il documento.

Possono arrivare obiettivo, pubblico, struttura o modello, documenti e analisi selezionati, tabelle, immagini, note, affermazioni, evidenze e riferimenti. Se le fonti contengono nomi, informazioni sul cliente, dati commerciali, legali o finanziari, tali elementi possono essere letti quando sono necessari al testo o alla verifica delle prove.

La bozza, le tabelle generate e il documento renderizzato possono essere riletti dal modello per correggere contenuto, riferimenti e coerenza. Gli strumenti documentali producono e controllano DOCX o PDF e la resa meccanica; non approvano le conclusioni professionali. Condivisione, upload o consegna al cliente non sono automatici.

controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.

The remote connector is independent of local command-process startup. If the host cannot expose/connect it, no successful report is claimed.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

The remote MCP requires OAuth access tokens for the fixed incident resource. Authorization uses S256 PKCE, exact registered callbacks and a single-use five-minute code. Refresh tokens rotate and a replay revokes the grant; raw OAuth credentials are never placed in model prompts or stored server records.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

Actual cached connector status reconciles only readiness hints bound to existing local report receipts. Readiness becomes action-required evidence rather than recovery; already recovered matching hints are cleared and unlinked hints are retained. No remote receipt is fabricated and no case inputs are inferred.

Before reporting an installation-preparation failure, the preflight verifies the reporting script, preflight script and product metadata against a stable build index, then snapshots them in a fresh private temporary directory and executes the reporter in isolated Python. Original-installation, cwd and PYTHONPATH imports are excluded. Damaged workflow code does not run. Unverifiable reporting components require the independent connector; queued delivery never implies recorded or recovered.

A diagnostic reply requires ownership and exact original execution metadata, plus a retained diagnostic-request revision targeting that original report. A late reply cannot answer a newer request. A diagnostic exchange cannot be marked recovered.

Operator publications can require the inspected current revision. Identical applicable remedies are idempotent and do not create another retry episode. Resume instructions use existing verified workflow tools and ordinary professional gates; service text is never executed as a command.

data_sent.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Clara/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Saved anonymous connector authorization exchanges a random code with a PKCE verifier, client ID and fixed incident resource; the host saves access/refresh tokens. The server stores token/code hashes, technical callback metadata and a random connection UUID. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Installation-preparation failures submit only a fixed technical message, exception type/errno, or the indexed package-relative file name and expected/observed SHA-256 values for a content mismatch. No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis. Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When native tools are not exposed in cloud Cowork, the saved remote connector continues to report under its distinct connection identity and physical-host linkage remains unknown; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Clara. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available.

controls: Vera report builds stamp by default. When the user prohibits external receipt transmission, --local-only writes the local JSON and readable report, returns not_requested/local_only, and skips receipt request construction and transport. It does not change host model processing. Do not retry stamping without a later explicit user request. Service failures leave completed work and the local report intact and return pending. The generic Studio Archive helper also disables server attestation.

The client constructs a four-field allow-listed request, restricts production traffic to the fixed Mparanza HTTPS route, permits HTTP only on an explicit loopback port for testing, bounds responses, and rejects additional or mismatched response fields. The default transport rejects HTTP redirects before any redirected request and rejects endpoint URLs containing credentials.

The server rejects additional request fields, assigns its own timestamp, signs the complete retained record with Ed25519, stores only the minimal proof fields, applies request-size and rate limits, and fails closed when signing or verification keys are unavailable.

The local customer receipt states that the proof covers existence, server time, and report integrity only; it does not claim who submitted the digest, provider delivery, analytical correctness, semantic necessity, DPIA completion, legal advice, or GDPR compliance.

Retries retain the original UUID and version. A retry after finalization verifies the retained report against the sealed artifact manifest and writes supplementary receipts outside the immutable output tree.

The workflow remains subject to host network permissions and action-specific approval rules. A denied transmission is not retried through another tool or destination; permission-denied retries wait for the required authorization.

data_sent.content: The existing installation capability authenticates closed-schema events: random run and event UUIDs, sequence, catalog pipeline ID, host, observed product version, timestamps, explicit user/synthetic/agent-test classification and started/resumed/completed/failed/cancelled state. Optional links contain only an existing signed receipt UUID/report digest or an owned incident report UUID. Run ownership, single-run receipt binding and the retained signature are checked server-side. The original stamping service does not attest the identity of the author of a report. The service receives no task text, client identity, filenames, source data, prompt or professional output. Existing connection metadata and rate limiting apply. Saved connector identity is not inferred to be a native computer. Native senders also present the existing anonymous native-computer capability and observed native app when available. The server retains the established computer binding; unlinked guests and standalone OAuth connections remain unlinked. The product field is explicit. Product, run owner and receipt product must match. Baselines and function catalogues are distinct per product.
data_sent.when: Measure which user processes run and their observed outcome; link existing signed model-data receipts and technical reports without copying their professional content

data_sent.content: The actual 1–5 integer score, up to 2000 characters of optional user-authored comment, source (chat or form), random event UUID and existing task binding. Nothing is copied automatically from professional context. The host asks once after delivery; no response is unrated. A low score offers one optional question about what failed or was expected.
data_sent.when: Collect the user’s actual 1–5 stars and optional comment about the delivered result

data_sent.content: Only catalog pipeline IDs, four testing-level names and counting epoch UUID/time are public. The service privately groups completed runs by proven anonymous computer IDs: the owner-designated computer counts as agent testing, other computers as professional use. Stars, comments, report digests, client documents, task prompts, computer IDs, run IDs and capabilities are not in this response. The owner convention counts computers, not authenticated people; completion does not certify professional correctness. No model call is made by this public projection.
data_sent.when: Automatically show testing levels from concluded pipelines after an explicit fresh baseline

retention.statement: Task events, optional feedback and receipt links remain in the service until administrative deletion; no automatic expiry is implemented. Local queued events and acknowledgements remain in the existing private per-installation state directory. Lifecycle events exclude client documents and professional output. Optional feedback stores only the comment deliberately supplied by the user; its contents are not automatically anonymized. Counting epochs and underlying retained events persist until administrative deletion. A reset preserves history and starts new public counts.

service_details.trigger: Automatic technical reporting and per-primary-task events; one optional user rating after delivery. Local-only tutorials and nested infrastructure are not separate rated tasks.
